items.title: Initial source pass
items.body: Opened IRS Topic 409, Topic 419, and Topic 559; Revenue Procedure 2025-32; IR-2025-103; IRC sections 61, 1256, and 165 via Cornell LII; FTB capital-gain page, conformity page, federal-change summary, 2025 rate schedules, and 2025 Form 540 instructions; CFTC Release 8302-20; Kalshi Klear's March 26, 2026 Regulation 39.5(b) filing; and Kalshi help articles dated June 21, 2026 and August 25, 2026.

items.title: Character left open
items.body: No IRS ruling naming event contracts was located. Section 1256 was not adopted as a default. Kalshi Klear's filing that event contracts are fully collateralized swaps and are not traded on margin was recorded as a fact against casual 60/40 claims, not as an IRS holding.

items.title: California nonconformity recorded
items.body: FTB states California has no lower capital-gain rate and does not conform to the federal 90 percent wagering-loss limitation in Public Law 119-21 section 70114. No final 2026 California individual rate schedule was located; the 2026 estimated-tax worksheet points to the 2025 tax table. 2025 FTB schedules are the rate tables used.

items.title: Practitioner seats left empty
items.body: No California Board of Accountancy record was matched to a published Kalshi-tax opinion. New Jersey license numbers printed on a practitioner website were not confirmed on the board portal in this pass. Those seats stay empty until a board lookup is completed and the published text is re-read.

items.title: Calculator added with tax-year guardrails
items.body: Added a 10,000-dollar step calculator through $200,000. The model uses the official 2026 federal ordinary rate schedule and the official 2025 California Schedule X. The selected amount is taxable income, not gross trading proceeds. Re-read the 2026 FTB Form 540-ES instructions: its worksheet tells filers to use the 2025 California tax table, so the California column is not labeled as a final 2026 return calculation.

items.title: Character comparison added to the calculator
items.body: Re-read Rev. Proc. 2025-32 section 4.01 Table 3 and section 4.03 (match the ledger); 26 U.S.C. section 1(h)(1) and section 1(j)(5) (new source irc-1, F47, F48); section 1256(a)(3), (b)(2)(B), (f)(2), and (g)(1) (F45, F46); FTB 2025 Schedule X (match; F49 rounding flag for rows at or below $100,000); FTB capital-gains page; Kalshi tax article (unchanged, 21 June 2026); IRS Topic 419 (still pre-2026 loss text, F27 stands). The calculator now computes five candidate characters from one slider: ordinary, short-term capital, section 1256 60/40, long-term capital, wagering. California is identical in every scenario. Static fallback rows are generated by scripts/render_calculator.py and checked by the validator against the JSON model.

items.title: Dated negative search and secondary conflicts
items.body: Site-restricted search of irs.gov for 'event contracts' and 'prediction market' returned nothing on point (F50). A request for a 2026 FTB rate-schedule PDF returned FTB's 404 page. Practitioner pages re-read: several state the IRS has issued no guidance and list the same candidate treatments; one asserts section 1256 and a $600 Form 1099-B as settled facts, contrary to Kalshi's own article; recorded on the flags page. No CPA seat was filled because no state-board lookup was completed.
